📌 Private Order Flow: Hiding a Trade Before Execution

Main Points
⏺ In a public mempool, other participants can see your transaction before confirmation
⏺ Private routing can hide an order from some bots and front-running strategies
⏺ This post explains why execution privacy matters for larger trades

1️⃣ Core Idea — a transaction is sent through a private channel or specialized executor instead of the public flow.
2️⃣ Why It Matters — it becomes harder for others to see your order early and jump ahead.
3️⃣ Where It Helps — large swaps, arbitrage, DeFi trades, and situations where price can worsen because of other actors.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — you now depend on a new execution route and its rules.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — understand who receives your transaction, how it is executed, and what guarantees the service provides.

Final Thoughts

Private order flow does not make execution perfect, but it can reduce the damage from public visibility. In crypto, it matters not only what you trade, but who sees it before it lands.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

Chaos at 30,000 Feet: Pilot Fight Sends Israel-Bound Jet Into Emergency Dive 🚨✈️


What began as a routine flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv turned into a terrifying midair emergency Wednesday after a violent confrontation erupted inside the cockpit of a Flydubai passenger jet.

Flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 bound for Israel with more than 150 passengers aboard, suddenly transmitted a series of emergency signals while flying over the region. One of the codes — 7500 — is internationally used to indicate unlawful interference and is commonly associated with a possible hijacking. Israeli authorities immediately treated the situation as a potential security threat, and fighter jets were scrambled.

The aircraft then changed course toward Saudi Arabia instead of continuing to Tel Aviv. Flight-tracking data showed a dramatic loss of altitude, adding to fears that something catastrophic was unfolding aboard the plane. 

The aircraft eventually landed safely at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia. All passengers were reported safe.

But the terrifying scenario was apparently not a hijacking.

 According to Israeli officials cited by Reuters, the emergency signals were triggered after the two pilots became involved in a physical fight inside the cockpit. The precise sequence of events remains under investigation.

Other reports have described an even more disturbing scene. Passengers reportedly heard shouting and saw blood, while some accounts claimed that one pilot may have stabbed the other. Those details have not been independently confirmed, and authorities have not publicly established what caused the confrontation or what the pilots intended.

For those on board, however, the distinction between a cockpit fight and a hijacking must have been meaningless in the moment.

The plane was thousands of feet above the ground. A distress code associated with hijacking had been transmitted. The aircraft was changing course, losing altitude and heading toward an emergency landing in a country that has no diplomatic relations with Israel.

Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz were brought into urgent consultations as the security system reacted to the unexplained emergency. 

Israeli fighter aircraft were dispatched toward the plane before the situation became clearer.

Flydubai confirmed that its flight had experienced an “incident” while en route to Tel Aviv and had been diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely. The airline said it was working with the relevant authorities to establish what happened.

The passengers were ultimately spared the worst. But the incident has raised extraordinary questions about what happened inside the cockpit of a commercial aircraft — and how a fight between two pilots could escalate into an emergency serious enough to trigger a hijacking alert and a military response.

For now, investigators face the task of reconstructing those critical minutes in the air.

One thing is already clear: for the passengers aboard FZ1073, a routine journey from Dubai to Israel suddenly became a fight for control at 30,000 feet.
